question: An otherwise healthy 16-year-old girl comes to the physician because she has not had a menstrual period. Examination shows normal breast development. There is coarse pubic and axillary hair. Pelvic examination shows a blind vaginal pouch. Ultrasonography shows normal ovaries and an atretic uterus. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of this patient's symptoms?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: End-organ insensitivity to androgens -> Lack of response to androgens -> Inadequate development of female reproductive structures -> Absence of menstrual periods -> 80%
CHAIN: Agenesis of the paramesonephric duct -> Failure of Müllerian duct development -> Absence of uterus and upper vagina -> Absence of menstrual periods -> 70%
analysis: Based on the presentation of primary amenorrhea with normal breast development, coarse pubic and axillary hair, blind vaginal pouch, atretic uterus, and normal ovaries, the most likely underlying cause is agenesis of the paramesonephric duct, also known as Müllerian agenesis or Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser syndrome.
